subtitle: Upendragupta and the Race to Carve Merit in Stone

panels.shot: epic wide of the Waghora gorge, caves glowing in late sun, Upendragupta in the foreground overlooking the cliff
panels.action: Upendragupta stands on a rocky ledge above the Waghora gorge, cloak stirring in the wind, as lines of workers swarm over the cliff where freshly carved cave façades gleam against dark forested hills.

dialogue.text: In Harishena’s age, a local lord named Upendragupta carved his faith into a cliff—yet his true rival was not an enemy army, but another patron racing to buy merit in stone.

i18n.hi: हर्षेण के ज़माने में, उपेन्द्रगुप्त नाम का एक स्थानीय राजा ने अपना धर्म चट्टान पर तराशा—पर उसका असली प्रतिद्वन्द्वी कोई दुश्मन सेना नहीं, बल्कि दूसरा दाता था जो पत्थर में पुण्य खरीदने दौड़ रहा था।

panels.shot: slow aerial sweep along the cliff, revealing multiple caves being cut at once
panels.action: An overhead view shows the Waghora gorge as a horseshoe of rock; scaffolds cling to the cliff where new caves are being hewn, while the river gleams far below in the monsoon light.

dialogue.text: The Ajanta cliff did not grow slowly. In a few charged decades around 460 CE, stone shook with hammers as many caves were cut at once, as if an entire world had rushed here.

i18n.hi: अजन्ता की चट्टान धीरे‑धीरे नहीं बढ़ी। करीब 460 ईसवी के कुछ उफनते दशकों में, पत्थर हथौड़ों से काँप उठा, कई गुफाएँ एक साथ कटीं—जैसे पूरा जग यहाँ टूट पड़ा हो।

panels.shot: close, low-angle on chisels striking rock, stone dust flying
panels.action: A team of artisans swing iron chisels into the rock face, sparks and powder leaping as rough pillars and doorways emerge from the living stone.

dialogue.text: This burst was no accident of piety alone. Inscriptions name the hands behind the gold and grain: ministers, feudatory rulers, and donors who turned devotion into stone walls and painted stories.

i18n.hi: ये विस्फोट सिर्फ भक्ति से नहीं हुआ। शिलालेख सोना‑अन्न देने वालों का नाम बताते हैं: मंत्री, सामन्त शासक, और दाता जो भक्ति को पत्थर की दीवारों और रंगी कहानियों में बदल गए।

panels.shot: interior wide of Cave 16 under construction, pillars half carved, a foreman pointing
panels.action: Inside a half-finished hall, rough pillars stand beside finely carved ones; a foreman gestures while sculptors work on elaborate capitals and painters outline faint figures on the plastered wall.

dialogue.text: At Cave 16, an inscription records a powerful buyer of merit: Varahadeva, minister of the Vakataka king Harishena, dedicating this vast vihara for the Buddha and for his own spiritual gain.

i18n.hi: गुफा 16 में एक लेख एक जबरदस्त पुण्य‑खरीदार का ज़िक्र करता है: वराहदेव, वाकाटक राजा हर्षेण का मंत्री, जो ये विराट विहार बुद्ध के लिए और अपने आध्यात्मिक लाभ के लिए अर्पित करता है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Upendragupta hearing news, a messenger bowing before him
panels.action: Upendragupta sits in a modest yet dignified hall, a scroll in his hand, while a travel-worn messenger bows, gesturing westward toward Ajanta.

dialogue.text: Not far away, a subordinate ruler under Harishena learned of this. His name, carved later in several caves, was Upendragupta—lord of this region, bound by duty and ambition.

i18n.hi: थोड़ी दूरी पर, हर्षेण के अधीन एक सामन्त को ये खबर लगी। उसका नाम, बाद में कई गुफाओं पर खुदा, था उपेन्द्रगुप्त—इस क्षेत्र का स्वामी, कर्तव्य और महत्वाकांक्षा से बँधा।

panels.shot: close-up on Upendragupta’s face, thoughtful, lit by lamplight
panels.action: In the warm glow of an oil lamp, Upendragupta leans over a palm-leaf manuscript, brows knit, the faint outline of a stupa diagram sketched beside his hand.

dialogue.speaker: upendragupta
dialogue.text: If a minister’s merit can take shape in rock… why should my cliff remain silent?

i18n.hi: अगर मंत्री का पुण्य चट्टान में रूप ले सकता है… तो मेरी चट्टान चुप क्यों रहे?

panels.shot: wide shot of Upendragupta arriving at Ajanta cliff with a small entourage
panels.action: Upendragupta, in courtly attire, stands at the edge of the Ajanta cliff with a few retainers and monks, gazing at the gorge as workers move below like ants.

dialogue.text: In an age when kingship and Buddhism intertwined, a cave was more than shelter. It was a public proclamation: of generosity, of rank, of closeness to the Dharma and to the throne.

i18n.hi: उस दौर में जब राजसत्ता और बौद्ध धर्म घुले मिले थे, गुफा सिर्फ आश्रय नहीं थी। वो सार्वजनिक घोषणा थी: दान की, ओहदे की, और धर्म व सिंहासन की नज़दीकी की।

panels.shot: medium shot of Upendragupta speaking with senior monks on the cliff edge
panels.action: On a flat ledge overlooking the gorge, Upendragupta confers with two senior monks in simple robes, one pointing toward a stretch of bare rock between existing caves.

dialogue.text: The monks knew the language of gifts. As later scholars like Gregory Schopen note, Buddhist merit was measured, recorded, and negotiated—names chiseled into stone as carefully as any statue.

i18n.hi: भिक्षु उपहारों की भाषा समझते थे। जैसे बाद के विद्वान ग्रेगरी स्कोपन बताते हैं, बौद्ध पुण्य नापा जाता, लिखा जाता, सौदा होता—नाम उतनी ही सावधानी से तराशे जाते जितनी से मूर्तियाँ।

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of the cliff section where Caves 17-20 will be, marked out by lines and stakes
panels.action: Workers mark the cliff with charcoal lines and wooden stakes, outlining four adjacent façades as Upendragupta watches, hands clasped behind his back.

dialogue.text: At this stretch of rock, later inscriptions would name Upendragupta as the donor behind multiple caves—17, 18, 19 and 20—turning a bare cliff into his field of merit.

i18n.hi: इस चट्टान की धार पर, बाद के लेख उपेन्द्रगुप्त को कई गुफाओं—17, 18, 19 और 20—के पीछे का दाता बताते हैं, एक सूनी चट्टान को उसके पुण्य‑क्षेत्र में बदलते हुए।

panels.shot: interior wide of Cave 17 under early excavation, central hall roughly blocked out
panels.action: Inside a raw, newly hewn space, rough columns are spaced out, and a distant rock wall hints at where a shrine will be; Upendragupta stands with an overseer, imagining the finished hall.

dialogue.text: Cave 17, a grand vihara, bears one of his dedicatory records. The inscription invokes the Buddha, the Sangha, and the benefit for all beings, but also clearly names the donor and his lineage.

i18n.hi: गुफा 17, एक भव्य विहार, उसके दान‑लेखों में से एक को सँभाले हुए है। लेख बुद्ध, संघ और सब प्राणियों के कल्याण का आह्वान करता है, पर दाता और उसकी वंशावली का नाम भी साफ दर्ज है।

panels.shot: medium shot of an artisan and scribe discussing with Upendragupta, a tablet showing layout
panels.action: A scribe kneels with a wax tablet showing a plan of cave walls, while a painter beside him holds a brush; Upendragupta listens, finger resting on his chin as they indicate where paintings might go.

dialogue.text: This was no random generosity. As Richard Cohen and others note, patrons shaped the very layout: size of halls, number of cells, even narrative cycles, aligning spiritual aims with social display.

i18n.hi: ये यूँ ही बिखरा दान नहीं था। रिचर्ड कोहेन व अन्य कहते हैं, दाताओं ने नक्शा तक गढ़ा: सभा‑कक्षों का आकार, कोशों की गिनती, यहाँ तक कि कथाचक्र—आध्यात्मिक लक्ष्य को सामाजिक जलवे से मिला कर।

panels.shot: montage-like wide shot inside Cave 17 with painters at work on Jataka murals
panels.action: Within the now-plastered hall, ladders lean against walls where painters apply rich pigments; faint Jataka scenes emerge—kings, cities, forests—while a monk watches quietly from a corner.

dialogue.text: As walls came alive with Jataka tales and Bodhisattvas, merit multiplied. The cave offered shelter to monks, instruction to lay visitors, and a visible stage where the donor’s devotion could be read.

i18n.hi: जैसे ही दीवारें जातक कथाओं और बोधिसत्त्वों से जीवित हुईं, पुण्य बढ़ता गया। गुफा ने भिक्षुओं को आश्रय दिया, गृहस्थों को सीख, और दाता के लिए एक खुला मंच, जहाँ उसकी भक्ति पढ़ी जा सके।

panels.shot: interior close on a mason chisel-carving an inscription panel frame
panels.action: A mason carefully smooths a rectangular panel by a doorway, preparing it as a framed space, while a scribe nearby practices letters on a palm leaf.

dialogue.text: Near doorways and pillars, blank panels awaited words. In time, they would carry inscriptions tying these works to Upendragupta and others—stone proof of who had given what, and why.

i18n.hi: द्वारों और स्तम्भों के पास, खाली पट्ट बने खड़े थे। समय के साथ उन पर लेख उकेरे गए जो इन कृतियों को उपेन्द्रगुप्त और अन्य से जोड़ते हैं—पत्थर‑सा सबूत कि किसने क्या और क्यों दिया।

panels.shot: medium shot of Upendragupta standing between two caves, works active on both sides
panels.action: Upendragupta stands on a scaffolded ledge between two caves, workers bustling on either side, while across the gorge the entrance of Cave 16 is also busy with activity.

dialogue.text: Opposite Varahadeva’s great Cave 16, Upendragupta’s cluster rose. Walter Spink has argued that such parallel projects formed a competition of generosity, each patron striving not to be outdone.

i18n.hi: वराहदेव की महान गुफा 16 के ठीक सामने, उपेन्द्रगुप्त का समूह उठा। वॉल्टर स्पिंक मानते हैं कि ऐसे समानान्तर प्रकल्प दान‑प्रतिस्पर्धा थे, जहाँ हर दाता पीछे न छूटने को आतुर था।

panels.shot: wide shot of Cave 19’s chaitya façade under construction, with its ornate front emerging
panels.action: The distinctive façade of Cave 19’s chaitya takes shape, its horseshoe arch carved deep and richly decorated, as workers hang from ropes to refine details; Upendragupta watches from below.

dialogue.text: Cave 19, with its richly ornate chaitya hall, also fell within his sphere. Its elegance—pillars, façade, and standing Buddha—speaks to a patron willing to invest heavily in beauty as merit.

i18n.hi: गुफा 19, अपनी आलंकारिक चैत्य‑सभा के साथ, भी उसके प्रभाव‑क्षेत्र में आई। इसकी नफ़ीसता—स्तम्भ, मुखौटा, और खड़े बुद्ध—एक ऐसे दाता को दिखाती है जो सौन्दर्य को ही भारी निवेश मानता था।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot of a small cave (like 18 or 20) with Upendragupta and a monk
panels.action: In a modest, smaller cave, a monk gestures to a simple shrine as Upendragupta bows slightly, the two sharing a quiet moment amid unfinished walls.

dialogue.text: Not every gift was grand. Smaller caves like 18 and 20, linked to his name, show that patronage could also be more intimate—spaces for recitation, meditation, and the daily rhythm of the Sangha.

i18n.hi: हर दान विराट नहीं था। 18 और 20 जैसी छोटी गुफाएँ, उससे जुड़ी हुई, दिखाती हैं कि संरक्षकता घनिष्ट भी हो सकती थी—पाठ, ध्यान और संघ के रोज़मर्रा जीवन के छोटे ठिकाने।

panels.shot: transition shot: split visual of Varahadeva’s inscription panel in Cave 16 and an inscription panel in Cave 17
panels.action: On one side, an inscription panel inside Cave 16 glows in lamplight; on the other, a similar panel in Cave 17, their surfaces filled with carefully chiseled Brahmi letters.

dialogue.text: Varahadeva, minister. Upendragupta, local ruler. Their inscriptions sit at eye level, equal in stone if not at court, each staking a claim in Ajanta’s sacred economy of gifts.

i18n.hi: वराहदेव, मंत्री। उपेन्द्रगुप्त, स्थानीय शासक। उनके लेख आँखों की ऊँचाई पर हैं—दरबार में भले बराबर न हों, पर पत्थर में बराबर, दोनों अजन्ता की पवित्र दान‑अर्थव्यवस्था में अपना दावा ठोंकते हुए।

panels.shot: medium shot of Upendragupta overseeing grain and coin being weighed and noted by scribes
panels.action: In a temporary camp near the caves, servants weigh sacks of grain and stacks of coins on a scale while scribes record lists; Upendragupta stands nearby, conferring with an accountant.

dialogue.text: Behind the serene images lay logistics. Endowments of land, grain, and coin kept masons fed, monks supported, lamps burning—tangible resources turned, through the Sangha, into spiritual credit.

i18n.hi: इन शान्त मूर्तियों के पीछे सारा बन्दोबस्त था। भूमि, अन्न और सिक्कों की उदारियाँ राजमिस्त्रियों का पेट भरतीं, भिक्षुओं को संभालतीं, दीपक जलाए रखतीं—ठोस संसाधन जो संघ के माध्यम से आध्यात्मिक पूँजी बनते।

panels.shot: wide, tense shot of Ajanta site with ominous sky, work seeming to slow
panels.action: Clouds gather dark over the gorge as some scaffolds stand idle, workers clustered uncertainly; unfinished caves show rough rock where polish was meant to be.

dialogue.text: Then, within a generation, the hammer blows faded. Harishena’s death shook the Vakataka order, and with the court’s fortunes, Ajanta’s great workshop fell suddenly silent.

i18n.hi: फिर, एक पीढ़ी के भीतर ही हथौड़ों की चोट थम गई। हर्षेण की मौत ने वाकाटक व्यवस्था हिला दी, और दरबार की किस्मत के साथ अजन्ता की महान कार्यशाला अचानक सूनी हो गई।

panels.shot: close-up on an unfinished sculpture in one of Upendragupta’s caves, features half formed
panels.action: A Buddha image inside a shrine stands only half carved; the face is smooth and blank where features should be, fine guidelines still visible on the rock.

dialogue.text: Spink and others see here the mark of a system: when elite patronage collapsed, projects stopped mid-stroke. The gift economy that had driven Ajanta’s frenzy could not sustain itself alone.

i18n.hi: स्पिंक व अन्य इसे पूरे तंत्र की निशानी मानते हैं: जैसे ही उच्च वर्ग का संरक्षण टूटा, काम अधबीच में रुक गया। जो दान‑अर्थव्यवस्था अजन्ता की दीवानगी चला रही थी, वो अकेले टिक नहीं सकी।

panels.shot: imagined reflective shot: older Upendragupta walking quietly through a completed hall
panels.action: In a calmer moment, Upendragupta walks barefoot through a finished Ajanta hall, hands folded, as monks chant softly in the dim, lamplit space.

dialogue.text: We do not know his final days. But we can still walk where he once stood, in halls that turned his wealth into shared refuge, his name into a quiet shadow at the edge of the murals.

i18n.hi: हम उसके अंतिम दिनों को नहीं जानते। पर हम अब भी वहाँ चल सकते हैं जहाँ वो कभी खड़ा था—उन सभागृहों में, जिन्होंने उसकी दौलत को साझा शरण में बदला, और उसके नाम को भित्तिचित्रों के किनारे हल्की परछाईं।

panels.shot: present-day style wide of Cave 17 interior, tourists small, murals towering
panels.action: Modern visitors stand tiny beneath Ajanta’s towering murals in Cave 17, their faces lifted toward ancient painted panels glowing softly in filtered light.

dialogue.text: Today, Cave 16 bears Varahadeva’s boast; Caves 17–20 remember Upendragupta. Ajanta’s splendour survives not one genius, but a network of patrons whose rivalry and faith carved a civilization into stone.

i18n.hi: आज गुफा 16 वराहदेव का दावा सँभाले है; गुफाएँ 17–20 उपेन्द्रगुप्त को याद रखती हैं। अजन्ता की शोभा किसी एक प्रतिभा की नहीं, बल्कि उन दाताओं के जाल की है, जिनकी होड़ और आस्था ने एक सभ्यता पत्थर में तराश दी।

title_i18n.hi: अजन्ता की गुफाओं का खर्च किसने उठाया

subtitle_i18n.en: Upendragupta and the Race to Carve Merit in Stone
subtitle_i18n.hi: उपेन्द्रगुप्त: पत्थर में पुण्य तराशने की दौड़
